findings.claim_or_location: Section C, section 4, line 38 -- Arem 2015 [11] '...no excess mortality appeared even at >=10x the minimum (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.59-0.78)'. The iter-2 remediation changed this point estimate from 0.68 to 0.69 (post-fix audit table row 2, line 100), citing iter-1 judge finding #2 and claiming '0.69 matches Arem 2015 source value'.
findings.issue: Regression introduced by the iter-2 remediation. Independently web-verified against the primary source PMID 25844730 / PMC4451435 (three confirmations: two PMC fetches plus a search hit citing the ASCO Post coverage of '32% lower mortality' = HR 0.68): the Arem 2015 >=10x-minimum (75+ MET-h/wk) hazard ratio is 0.68 (95% CI 0.59-0.78), NOT 0.69. The iter-1 judge finding #2 ('Arem >=10x HR rounding 0.68->0.69') was itself incorrect about the source value, and the author complied, replacing a previously-correct 0.68 with an incorrect 0.69. The CI (0.59-0.78) and the load-bearing 'no harm ceiling at very high volume' framing remain fully supported; this is a 0.01 point-estimate error on a non-load-bearing value, but it is now a genuine source-mismatch where iter-1 was correct. Note the coincidental collision the author flagged on line 117: the recommended-minimum (1x, 7.5-<15 MET-h/wk) HR genuinely IS 0.69 (95% CI 0.67-0.70) per the source and is correct -- only the >=10x value is wrong.
findings.recommended_fix: Revert the >=10x point estimate from 0.69 back to 0.68 (95% CI 0.59-0.78) to match the Arem 2015 source. Leave the 1x recommended-minimum HR at 0.69 (0.67-0.70) -- that one is source-correct. Update the post-fix audit table (line 100) to record that iter-1 finding #2 was based on an erroneous source value and is reverted, so the audit trail does not re-encode the wrong value.
